title: The unit circle and exact values

points.text: cos and sin as coordinates on the unit circle; tan as sin/cos
Exact values at 0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2 and their multiples
The ambiguous case of the sine rule

bigPicture: The unit circle defines sin and cos for every angle, so trig works beyond 90°. Paper 1 relies on exact values.

keyIdeas.answer: A point at angle θ is (cos θ, sin θ); tan θ = sin θ / cos θ.
sin: 0, ½, √2/2, √3/2, 1 at 0, π/6, π/4, π/3, π/2 (cos reversed); tan π/4 = 1, tan π/6 = 1/√3, tan π/3 = √3. Signs by quadrant (CAST).
Given a, b and non-included A with a < b, sin B may give an acute and an obtuse B (180° − B); check both fit (angle sum < 180°).

keyTerms.def: quadrants where cos, all, sin, tan are positive

misconceptions.wrong: Ambiguous case always has two answers
misconceptions.right: Only if 180° − B still fits the triangle.

practice.prompt: Find exactly sin(4π/3), cos(7π/4) and tan(2π/3).
In triangle ABC, AB = 10, BC = 7, angle A = 40°. Find the two possible values of angle C.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.

linkingQuestions.prompt: How does the unit circle give every solution of sin x = k in an interval?
